assets.name: Parade Animal Cards
assets.purpose: Reusable physical cards used by pairs to build, manipulate, read, translate, and fix parade patterns. The core manipulative of the entire unit — used in every lesson by every pair. In Grade 1 the teacher may add small letter stickers (A, B, C) to selected cards to bridge animals to rule labels during Lesson 2.
assets.page_layout: Two letter pages, portrait orientation, each holding 8 cards in a 2x4 grid. Each card is approximately 3in × 3in with thin solid cut-lines between cards. The 16-card set contains 4 of each animal: Bea (solid vest), Finn (striped vest), Bibi (dotted vest), Moss (checkered vest). Page 1 holds 4 Bea + 4 Finn cards; page 2 holds 4 Bibi + 4 Moss cards.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in square B&W line-art card showing Bea the Bear in cartoon style: simple bold outlines, brown fur indicated by short hatching, friendly smile, wearing a small vest filled with a SOLID dark pattern (so Bea is visually distinct from the other animals' vests in B&W). Centred on the card with a thin black border. The animal fills about 80% of the card. Same stroke weight and proportions as Finn, Bibi, and Moss.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 portion of page 1.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in square B&W line-art card showing Finn the Fox in matching style: simple bold outlines, friendly smile, wearing a small vest filled with HORIZONTAL STRIPES (so Finn's vest is visually distinct from the other animals in B&W). Centred, thin black border. Identical stroke weight to Bea, Bibi, Moss.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 portion of page 1.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in square B&W line-art card showing Bibi the Beaver in matching style: simple bold outlines, paddle tail visible, friendly smile, wearing a small vest filled with DOTS / POLKA-DOT pattern (so Bibi's vest is visually distinct from the other animals in B&W). Centred, thin black border. Same stroke weight.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 portion of page 2.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in square B&W line-art card showing Moss the Moose in matching style: simple bold outlines, small antlers, friendly smile, wearing a small vest filled with a CHECKERED / GRID pattern (so Moss's vest is visually distinct from the other animals in B&W). Centred, thin black border. Same stroke weight.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 portion of page 2.

teacher_prep_steps: Print both pages (one set per pair — for a class of 20 print 10 sets = 20 pages).
Optional but strongly recommended: laminate before cutting, so the cards survive Grade 1 hands across multiple lessons.
Cut along the thin solid lines into 16 individual 3in × 3in cards per set.
Store each set in a labelled zip-top bag or envelope ('Parade Animal Cards — Pair 1', etc.).

Optional Grade 1 prep: cut a small sheet of round letter stickers (A, B, C) and keep them with the teacher's set — to be applied temporarily to a few cards during Lesson 2 as a bridge between animals and rule labels. Peel off after the lesson.

Optional colour suggestion: if you have a colour printer and the budget for it, you may colour-print so each animal's vest is its named colour (Bea = red, Finn = blue, Bibi = green, Moss = yellow). The unit works equally well in B&W because each vest also has a unique pattern fill (solid, stripes, dots, checkered) that distinguishes the four animals visually.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 set (16 cards) per pair = 10 sets for a class of 20 students.

assets.name: Blank Parade Strip
assets.purpose: A printable strip with 5 cells that pairs use to lay out animal cards, build patterns, and visualize the parade route. In Grade 1 the strip is also used for NUMBER parades — children write whole numbers (up to 50) into the cells with dry-erase markers (Lesson 5). The teacher uses larger versions of the same strip during whole-group circle time.
assets.page_layout: Letter page, landscape orientation, with 2 horizontal parade strips stacked (one above, one below). Each strip is 5 cells wide, each cell ~1.5in square, with footprint icons drawn faintly beneath. A thin solid cut-line separates the two strips.

image_placeholders.description: A horizontal 5-cell parade strip in B&W line-art style. Each cell is approximately 1.5in × 1.5in with a solid light-grey border, sized to hold a 1.4in animal card or sticker — or a hand-written 2-digit number — comfortably. Below the cells, faintly drawn footprints suggest a parade route from left to right. The whole strip is approximately 8in wide × 2in tall. Identical to the strip layout used in the worksheets so children recognize it immediately.
image_placeholders.placement: Printed twice per page (top half and bottom half), separated by a thin solid cut line.

teacher_prep_steps: Print enough pages to yield ~12 strips (one per pair plus 2 spare = 6 pages, since each page produces 2 strips).
Laminate the pages — this is essential for Grade 1 because Lesson 5 requires writing numbers on the strips with dry-erase markers.
Cut along the horizontal cut line between the two strips on each page.
Distribute one strip per pair; keep 2 extras at the teacher table for whole-group demonstrations.
Bring a class set of dry-erase markers and a small cloth for erasing — needed for the Lesson 5 number parade.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 strip per pair plus 2 spare for the teacher's whole-group demos = 12 strips total for a class of 20.

assets.name: Sound and Movement Cards
assets.purpose: An 8-card set used by the class and by pairs to translate visual rules into auditory and kinesthetic rules. Used in Lesson 3 (Same Rule, Different Parade — 5 pair sets) and Lesson 5 (summative, available as an option for the body translation).
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with 8 cards in a 2x4 grid. Each card is approximately 3in × 3in. Cards depict: clap (open hand), stomp (footprint), jump (jumping figure), freeze (hand up, palm out), hum (musical note + lips), tap (finger on surface), wave (waving hand), spin (circular arrow). Thin solid cut-lines between cards.

image_placeholders.description: A 3in × 3in card showing two open hands meeting — the universal clap icon. Simple, bold B&W line art, child-friendly. Word 'CLAP' printed beneath the icon in clear K/G1-readable type.
A 3in × 3in card showing a single footprint pressed firmly into the ground — the stomp icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'STOMP' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing a stick figure with arms up and feet off the ground — the jump icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'JUMP' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing a stick figure standing perfectly still with one hand up, palm facing out — the freeze icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'FREEZE' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing closed lips with a small musical note hovering above — the hum icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'HUM' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing a single finger lightly tapping a surface, with two small motion lines — the tap icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'TAP' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing an open hand mid-wave with two small motion lines — the wave icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'WAVE' printed beneath.
A 3in × 3in card showing a circular arrow indicating rotation — the spin icon. Simple bold line art. Word 'SPIN' printed beneath.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 6 pages total: 1 for the teacher's whole-group set + 5 for partner sets in Lesson 3 (Grade 1 pairs use the cards directly during translation, not just the teacher).
Laminate the pages for durability.
Cut along the cut-lines into 8 individual cards per set.
Store each set in a labelled envelope. Bring all 6 sets to Lesson 3; bring the teacher set only to Lesson 5.
Optional colour suggestion: B&W works well; print in colour only if you specifically want extra visual variety for whole-group circle time.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 teacher set + 5 partner sets (8 cards each) = 6 sets for a class of 20.

assets.name: Missing Mystery Card
assets.purpose: A small card showing a question mark inside a dotted outline. Placed in a parade strip to indicate that an animal (or number) is missing from that position. Used heavily in Lesson 4 (Detective Parade) and available in Lesson 5 for challenge mode.
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with 12 cards in a 3x4 grid. Each card is approximately 2in × 2in (smaller than the animal cards so it visually 'belongs' inside an empty cell). Identical design on every card.

image_placeholders.description: A 2in × 2in square card with a thin solid border. Inside, a dashed-outline rectangle filling about 80% of the card. Inside that dashed rectangle, a large bold question mark (~1in tall) drawn in dark grey or black. Simple, instantly recognizable to a Grade 1 student as 'something is missing here'. Identical on every card on the page.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 5 pages (60 cards = 5 cards per pair × 10 pairs + spares).
Laminate before cutting.
Cut along the cut-lines into individual 2in × 2in cards.
Distribute 5 cards per pair before Lesson 4.
assets.quantity_per_class: 5 cards per pair = 50 cards = 5 printed pages for a class of 20.

assets.name: Core Loop Frame
assets.purpose: A reusable physical frame that students place over the repeating part of a parade strip to mark and isolate the core. In Grade 1, after circling the core, the child writes the rule label (AB, ABB, etc.) on a sticky note and places it next to the loop. Used in Lesson 2 (rule-naming), Lesson 3 (verifying same-rule-different-rep), Lesson 4 (using the rule to fix gaps), and Lesson 5 (summative).
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with 4 oval/lasso frames in a 2x2 grid. Each oval is approximately 4in wide × 1.7in tall, designed to frame a 2-, 3-, or sometimes 4-cell core comfortably. Each oval has a thin solid outer line and a thicker inner-edge line for visual emphasis. Cut-lines around each oval.

image_placeholders.description: A horizontal oval frame approximately 4in wide × 1.7in tall, drawn as a thick black outline (about 4pt) on a white interior. The shape is a clean ellipse — wide and short, so it can be placed over 2 or 3 cells of a parade strip without occluding the animal icons inside. No fill, no shadow, no decoration — just the frame outline.
image_placeholders.placement: Repeated 4 times in a 2x2 grid on the page.

teacher_prep_steps: Print on cardstock if available — durability matters because pairs handle these repeatedly.
Alternative: print on regular paper and laminate.
Cut around the outside of each oval to produce 4 frames per page (3 pages = 12 frames for a class of 20 = ~1 per pair plus spares).
Distribute one frame per pair before Lesson 2.

Provide a small pad of sticky notes per pair — Grade 1 children write the rule label (AB / ABB / AAB / ABC) on a sticky and place it next to the loop. This is new in Grade 1; in K the loop alone was the marker.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 frame per pair plus 2 spares = 12 frames = 3 pages for a class of 20.

assets.name: Coco the Conductor Puppet
assets.purpose: A printable Coco illustration that the teacher mounts on a popsicle stick to use as the recurring class character throughout all 5 lessons. Coco hosts each circle time, holds up the parade strips, and asks the new Grade 1 question 'How do you KNOW?' to push children toward justification.
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with a single large Coco illustration (~7in tall) and a small rectangular tab (~1in × 3in) at the bottom for the popsicle stick to be glued or taped behind. A thin cut-line traces the outside of Coco's silhouette including the tab.

image_placeholders.description: A full-body B&W line-art cartoon illustration of Coco the Conductor, approximately 7in tall: a friendly parrot with bold simple outlines, feather details indicated with line-art hatching (no fill), big round eyes, a warm smile, holding a small wooden conductor's baton in one wing. Slightly stylized, Grade 1-appropriate, no scary or sharp features. At the bottom of the illustration, a small rectangular tab (~1in × 3in) extends below Coco's feet — this is for gluing the popsicle stick behind. A thin cut-line traces the outside of Coco's body including the tab. Visually identical to the Kindergarten Coco so a child returning from K recognizes him.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 page on cardstock if possible (or regular paper + laminate for durability).
Cut around the outside of Coco's silhouette including the bottom tab.
Glue or tape a popsicle stick or tongue depressor behind the bottom tab so Coco can be held up like a puppet.
Optional: laminate before cutting for years of reuse.
Store flat in a folder so the puppet doesn't crease.

Optional colour suggestion: the design is intentionally B&W line art so any printer can produce it. If you have a colour printer, print in colour. Alternatively — and this is a lovely Day-0 activity — give children the B&W Coco and have them colour it together as a class before Lesson 1, with red and yellow feathers as the canonical palette.

assets.name: Anchor Chart Word Cards
assets.purpose: A printable set of four word cards (PATTERN, CORE, MISSING, EXTEND) with child-voice definitions and small visual cues. The teacher tapes each card to the class anchor chart as the corresponding word is introduced across the unit. In Grade 1 the teacher additionally hand-prints two more cards on chart paper (RULE during Lesson 2 and JUSTIFY during Lesson 4) — the printed set covers the cross-grade vocabulary, while the hand-printed additions capture the Grade 1 leap.
assets.page_layout: One letter page, portrait orientation, with 4 word cards in a 2x2 grid. Each card is approximately 3.5in × 4.5in. Each card has the WORD in large bold uppercase at the top, the child-voice definition underneath in smaller K/G1-readable type, and a small visual cue icon in the corner. Thin solid cut-lines between cards.

image_placeholders.description: A 3.5in × 4.5in word card. Large bold uppercase 'PATTERN' centred at the top (~1.2in tall lettering). Below the word, in clear K/G1-readable type (~0.4in tall): 'Something that repeats in the same order.' In the lower-right corner, a small clap-stomp icon pair (~0.8in tall). Thin black border around the card. B&W line art only.

A 3.5in × 4.5in word card. Large bold uppercase 'CORE' centred at the top. Below: 'The little part of the pattern that keeps repeating.' Lower-right corner: a small Core Loop Frame icon (~0.8in tall) — the lasso/oval shape — matching the M5 manipulative. Thin black border. B&W line art only.

A 3.5in × 4.5in word card. Large bold uppercase 'MISSING' centred at the top. Below: 'A part of the parade that is not there yet — we use the rule to figure it out.' Lower-right corner: a small question-mark-in-dashed-box icon (~0.8in tall) matching the M4 Missing Mystery Card design. Thin black border. B&W line art only.

A 3.5in × 4.5in word card. Large bold uppercase 'EXTEND' centred at the top. Below: 'To keep the pattern going forwards or backwards using the rule.' Lower-right corner: a small bidirectional arrow icon (~0.8in tall) — a left arrow and a right arrow joined, representing extension in both directions. Thin black border. B&W line art only.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 page (1 set per class is enough — these go on the wall, not in pair bags).
Laminate the page for durability before cutting; this set will last for next year's class too.
Cut along the cut-lines into 4 individual word cards.
On Day 1, after introducing 'pattern', tape the PATTERN card to your anchor chart paper.
On Day 2, after introducing 'core' and 'rule', tape the CORE card; hand-print 'RULE' on chart paper beside it (the Grade 1 addition).
On Day 4, after introducing 'missing' and 'extend' and 'justify', tape both MISSING and EXTEND cards; hand-print 'JUSTIFY' on chart paper.
Save the laminated set in a folder labelled 'Pattern Parade — Anchor Words' for re-use next year.

overall_prep_notes: Total prep time across all 7 assets: approximately 105 minutes for a class of 20 — slightly more than Kindergarten because Grade 1 pairs use sound/movement cards directly in Lesson 3 (5 partner sets vs K's 1 teacher set). Default print spec is BLACK AND WHITE for every asset — this ensures any printer in any classroom can produce the unit. Colour printing is suggested in several assets (M1, M3, Coco) for visual richness only; the unit works equally well in B&W because animal vests use distinct pattern fills (solid / stripes / dots / checkered) and Coco is line art. Recommended prep approach: prep the entire unit's manipulatives in one sitting before Lesson 1 — front-loads the work but means the unit runs smoothly day-to-day. Critical: laminate M2 parade strips because Lesson 5 requires writing numbers on them with dry-erase markers. Storage: keep all sets in a labelled bin or shelf, with each pair's set in its own bag. The animal cards (M1) are by far the most-used asset — laminate these even if you skip lamination on others.
